title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: love of justice requires no one be loved in Christ unto actual fruitful share of salvation before persevering faith — yet may be loved unto eternal preparation of salvation before being considered as believing
pass_a_gloss: That I may contract our response into few words, I say that the love of justice requires that no one be loved in Christ unto salvation, unless he who by faith has apprehended him; but in this sense, that he by no means be loved unto the actual and fruitful participation of salvation before he shall have persevered in faith, yet he can be loved unto the everlasting preparation of salvation in the Divine mind and will before he be considered as believing and persevering in this faith. For the very preparation of faith and of perseverance are arguments of Divine love: but they are prepared before they are infallibly foreseen in Peter as infallibly about to be. And these saving gifts are prepared to be infallibly conferred upon singular persons, not except from a love looking unto their salvation. Nor in this preparation is God to be thought to violate the laws of his justice, but to unfold the riches of his special mercy.
pass_b_english: To put our answer in few words: love of justice requires that no one be loved in Christ unto salvation unless he has apprehended him by faith. Take that in this sense: he is not loved unto actual fruitful share of salvation before he has persevered in faith — yet he can be loved unto the eternal preparation of salvation in God's mind and will before he is considered as believing and persevering in that faith. For the very preparation of faith and perseverance are marks of divine love: they are prepared before they are infallibly foreseen in Peter as infallibly about to be. And these saving gifts are prepared to be infallibly conferred on singular persons only from a love that looks to their salvation. In that preparation God is not to be thought to violate the laws of his justice, but to unfold the riches of his special mercy.
source_text: Ut in pauca contraham responsionem nostram, dico, Amorem justitiae requirere ut nemo in Christo ad salutem ametur, nisi qui fide ipsum apprehenderit; sed hoc sensu, ut minime ametur ad actualem et fructuosam participationem salutis priusquam in fide perseveraverit, amari tamen possit ad aeternam salutis in mente et voluntate Divina preparationem priusquam consideretur ut credens et in hac fide perseverans. Nam ipsa praeparatio fidei et perseverantiae sunt amoris Divini argumenta: praeparantur autem prius quam infallibiliter praevidentur in Petro infallibiliter futurae. Atque praeparantur haec dona salutifera singularibus personis infallibiliter conferenda, non nisi ex amore ad salutem illorum spectante. Neque in hac praeparatione Deus violare putandus est leges justitiae suae, sed explicare opes specialis misericordiae suae.
